correctness.rationale: The incidence graph is cubic on 18 vertices, so any dominating set has at least 5 vertices. Point-side/line-side coverage inequalities force any 5-set split to be (2,3) or (3,2); equality forces exactly the nine point-centered B and nine line-centered A configurations. Pairwise incidence calculations give concurrence 0 for 27 edges, 1 for 72 same-side pairs and 2 for 54 cross-shore nonedges, with every coordinate occurring in five hypotheses. This proves the polynomial 1+18z+126z^2 and prohibits shattered triples. The connected one-dimensional complex has integral Betti rank 126-18+1=109. Every query has five positive hypotheses, excluding adaptive depth four, and a point query then nonincident/incident line queries yields four groups of sizes 2,3,5,8, each divisible by a final coordinate query, witnessing depth three. Independent Python and C++17 programs reproduced all 18 optima and trace counts; C++17 enumerated all 262143 nonempty vertex subsets.

value.rationale: The Pappus graph is a canonical, highly symmetric point-line incidence graph. Its minimum dominating sets form an exact eighteen-block design whose coordinate concurrence reconstructs every graph edge. The same design supplies a motivated learning invariant with a strict VC/Littlestone gap and an exact integral shattering homotopy type. The result connects graph domination, incidence reconstruction and adaptive learning by explicit structural theorems rather than an arbitrary finite tabulation.
